result.question: Why does the king think Arameans left?

readings.answer: Because they know the people in the city are starving.
readings.support: They know we are starving, so they have left the camp

readings.answer: To capture the people when they come out and enter the city.
readings.support: thinking, ‘When they come out of the city, we will take them alive and enter the city.’
left the camp to hide in the field

assessments.reason: The king explicitly says, “They know we are starving, so they have left the camp,” which is a stated causal reason, though it omits the ambush/conquest purpose in the key.
“When they come out of the city, we will take them alive and enter the city” matches the idea of ambushing the Israelites and taking the city.
“They have left the camp to hide in the field” is directly stated as the reason for leaving, though it does not include the subsequent goal of capture/entry mentioned in the key.

result.reason: The text supplies several distinct ‘why’ reasons (knowledge of starvation, to hide in the field, and to capture and enter the city), so more than one materially different answer fits.
